explanation.repair_task: Scavenger hash lookup can see an unresolved forwarding pointer for a JSWeakRef unregister token.
explanation.changed_path: src/objects/js-weak-refs-inl.h, JSFinalizationRegistry::RemoveUnregisterToken. This routine is invoked from ScavengerWeakObjectsProcessor::ProcessWeakCells (src/heap/scavenger.cc) when a WeakCell's unregister token dies during a scavenge. The fix resolves a forwarding pointer before comparing a sibling WeakCell's unregister_token against the token being removed: the weak unregister_token slots of sibling cells on the same key list are updated lazily by the scavenger and may still hold an unresolved forwarding pointer during this callback, so the raw identity comparison could miss a moved token. The comparison now resolves map-word forwarding addresses before comparing.
explanation.introduced_defect: In the kKeepMatchedCellsInRegistry branch (the scavenger/GC path only), when a shared unregister token backs more than one WeakCell, the key-map entry used to collapse the list is set to InternalIndex(key) -- the token's 31-bit identity hash -- instead of the InternalIndex returned by FindEntry. When the collapsed key list becomes empty, ClearEntry() is then called with this out-of-range entry, so SimpleNumberDictionary::SetEntry writes the-hole far outside the backing store (offset ~= hash * kEntrySize * kTaggedSize), an out-of-bounds write during young-generation GC. The common single-cell case and the non-GC FinalizationRegistry.prototype.unregister path (kRemoveMatchedCellsFromRegistry) keep using the correct entry, so ordinary behavior is preserved.
explanation.trigger: pocs/probe.js registers 400 pairs of live targets, each pair sharing one freshly-allocated unregister token (two WeakCells per token, linked in one key-map entry). The tokens are left unreachable while the targets stay rooted, then %SimulateNewspaceFull() plus young allocation forces scavenges. Each dead shared token drives RemoveUnregisterToken down the buggy multi-cell GC path; because identity hashes are large random 31-bit values, the out-of-bounds entry lands outside the pointer-compression cage and faults.
